messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: P0 — Dedicated pool 'acorn-dedicated-us-west' GPU saturation. tenant=acorn_health tenant-id=T-CH-042. 100% GPU util on all 8 cards for 12m, request failures and 429s observed. Paging oncall.
oncall_alex: I'm on. grabbing current metrics and scaling logs.
oncall_alex: summary from metrics: all 8 GPUs pinned, queue length spike, latency up ~3x for that tenant only. No cross-tenant impact? seeing errors only from acorn_health.
cust_success_maya: Maya (CS) here — I just told Acorn support team we're investigating. They confirm degraded UX, customers report timeouts during uploads.
infra_lee: checking autoscaler logs. Looks like cluster couldn't provision new instances — hit GCP GPU quota in us-west1 for project-redwood-dedicated. Also a startup error on one node: nvidia-driver timeout.
eng-platform_jess: if quota is the blocker we have two quick mitigations: 1) enable burst into shared pool (non-dedicated) for acorn while we request quota, or 2) apply model-fallback to a smaller quantized variant for that tenant. Both have tradeoffs.
oncall_alex: Jess — can we route just this tenant to shared pool without exposing other tenants to their data? Need isolation posture. What's the privacy impact?
eng-platform_jess: we can route via per-tenant network segmentation and token-scope filter. Shared pool supports VPC egress isolation via proxy; data remains encrypted. It's not ideal but acceptable for emergency. Will require a config flip: set routing.policy=burst_shared_for:tenant:T-CH-042. 30s change.
cust_success_maya: I'll get Acorn's permission for temporary routing. They asked for ETA on mitigation.
sales_eddie: cc'ing account team — they need to know if SLA hit. This is a paid Dedicated contract with 99.9% uptime SLA. Keep me posted.
engineer_priya: also we can instantly reduce concurrency by 50% for that tenant at the API gateway (throttle) to reduce load and buy time. granular per-tenant throttles exist.
dataplane_sam: I can flip the throttle now and start a rolling driver restart to clear the stuck KV caches. Which do you prefer, throttle or burst?
oncall_alex: do throttle first. Less blast radius. Set throttle to concurrency: 2 and max_tokens_per_minute reduced.
dataplane_sam: executing now: ```sh
# reduce concurrency for tenant T-CH-042
redwoodctl routing set-rate --tenant T-CH-042 --concurrency 2 --tpm 2000
``` 
dataplane_sam: throttle applied. seeing queue drop by ~30%.
infra_lee: started driver restart on node gpu-5 to clear possible memory leak. Rolling restart, 1 node at a time.
eng-platform_jess: filing burst change as a canary: I'll prepare a policy and smoke test. If throttle doesn't stabilize within 5m we'll open burst.
oncall_alex: status check in 5. Also request oncall escalation to infra if node restart fails.
incident-bot: incident-bot: Incident state -> INVESTIGATING. Priority -> P0. Acknowledge: oncall_alex. Timeline: 12m since alert.
cust_success_maya: Acorn agrees to temporary routing while we work on permanent fix. They want rollback once stable.
infra_lee: node restart succeeded on gpu-5, driver came up clean. Utilization shifted to remaining nodes but some requests recovered.
oncall_alex: good. throttle + restart + partial recovery = OK. Jess, please prepare burst config in case quota request delays.
eng-platform_jess: prepared draft policy. To enable burst we need two things: set routing.policy.burst=true for tenant and spin up 2x  A100 preemptible nodes in shared pool. I can trigger, but need ops approval for cost.
sales_eddie: authorize costs for emergency burst, prioritize SLA + customer retention.
engineer_priya: small risk: shared pool uses different kernel/hardware; may see 1-2% perf diff. We'll mark as 'best-effort' in logs.
dataplane_sam: ready to flip routing if you give the go. Also prepping fallback model variant path: /models/redwood-lite-4q.
oncall_alex: go ahead with burst. Jess, flip the routing, Sam, stand by to route traffic. Priya, push a notice to k8s events if model fallback used.
eng-platform_jess: triggering burst now: ```yaml
# applying emergency burst for tenant T-CH-042
routing:
  tenant: T-CH-042
  policy:
    burst: true
    target_pool: shared-gpu-burst-us-west
``` 
eng-platform_jess: burst applied. spinning two preemptible A100s.
incident-bot: incident-bot: external-comms suggested: "We are routing your workload to temporary burst capacity to restore service while we resolve dedicated pool capacity. No data will be shared with other tenants." (posted to Acorn)
cust_success_maya: Acorn confirms partial restoration — they see lower 500s and improved throughput.
infra_lee: new preemptible nodes online, join cluster, drivers okay. load balancing feels even.
oncall_alex: monitoring latency and error rate for that tenant — trending down. nice work team.
engineer_priya: we'll do a follow-up: root cause is spike plus insufficient headroom + quota blocking autoscaler. Short-term mitigation = burst + throttle. Long-term: request quota increase, revisit autoscaler fallback logic, add pre-approved emergency burst to contract.
sales_eddie: please include cost estimate for the burst hours in the post-incident summary. Also notify legal/finance for chargeback rules.
incident-bot: incident-bot: Incident state -> MITIGATED. Next steps: postmortem + customer-comms draft. Assigned: eng-platform_jess, infra_lee, cust_success_maya.
oncall_alex: leaving a log entry and handing off to eng-platform for postmortem. I'm clear for now. :white_check_mark:
cust_success_maya: I'll draft email to Acorn thanking them and explaining temporary measures + timeline for permanent fixes.
eng-platform_jess: capturing runbook updates: add per-tenant burst toggle, pre-approve cost cap, and autoscaler QoS improvements. Will file RFC.
incident-bot: incident-bot: Timeline: alert 1717456660, mitigated 1717457110, duration ~9m. Closing thread to live follow-up.
